credentials.title: Registered Credentials
credentials.intro: The keys this device holds. Privasys account keys cannot be re-created by signing in again. Removing one locks that account until recovery.

credentials.accountSwitchedBody: Sign-ins from this device will now use {{account}}.
credentials.removeKeyBody:
This is the key to your Privasys {{account}}.

Removing it permanently discards this device’s only way to prove that identity. Signing in again will NOT restore it: a new registration creates a NEW, empty account. Everything bound to this account (app ownership, roles, vault approvals) stays locked until you run account recovery with its recovery phrase.

Only remove this if you are certain the account is disposable or safely held elsewhere.
credentials.removeActiveKeyBody:
This is the key to your Privasys {{account}}, the one your sign-ins currently use.

Removing it permanently discards this device’s only way to prove that identity. Signing in again will NOT restore it: a new registration creates a NEW, empty account. Everything bound to this account (app ownership, roles, vault approvals) stays locked until you run account recovery with its recovery phrase.

Only remove this if you are certain the account is disposable or safely held elsewhere.
credentials.removeCredentialBody: Remove the passkey for {{host}}? You will register again the next time you sign in to that app; anything stored under your current identity there may not carry over.
credentials.removeAllBodyWithAccounts_one: This removes all {{total}} credentials, including {{count}} Privasys account key. Those accounts become unreachable until account recovery: a fresh sign-in creates new, empty identities, not the old ones. Continue?

firstConnect.card1Body: {{app}} wants to connect to your wallet. Before you decide, here is what your wallet just did on your behalf. It takes about a minute.
firstConnect.card2Title: Your wallet checked the app, not the company
firstConnect.card2WebBody: A padlock proves you reached the right company's server. After that, you trust the company.
firstConnect.card2HereBody: The chip itself signed a statement of exactly which code is running. Your wallet checked it against the code the developer published.
firstConnect.card3Title: Nobody can look inside. Including us
firstConnect.card3Body: The app runs in memory that the machine's own operator cannot read. The servers {{app}} sits on use hardware-sealed enclaves, so nobody running them can open your files.
firstConnect.card3Aside: That is a property of the hardware, not a promise in a policy.
firstConnect.card4Title: You stay in charge, and you can check again
firstConnect.card4Body: Your wallet remembers this exact code. If a single byte of it changes, you get asked again and shown what changed.
firstConnect.card4Aside: You can make any app prove itself live, and you can withdraw access at any time.
firstConnect.watchIntro: Three things worth knowing before you allow anything.
firstConnect.watchLiveTitle: A request you did not expect is a request to reject
firstConnect.watchLiveBody: Approvals happen in real time. Every one should be the result of something you just did, like scanning a code or opening a link. If one arrives on its own, reject it.
firstConnect.watch1Body: Anyone can call their app anything. The address and the developer are the parts that are hard to fake, and they are the parts to read.
firstConnect.watch2Title: “We could not check this app” is not a pass
firstConnect.watch2Body: It means we got no answer. Continuing puts you back on ordinary-internet trust, which is where you already live everywhere else.
firstConnect.watch3Title: An app that changed is normal, and is exactly when to look
firstConnect.watch3Body: Updates happen often. The screen will show you what changed. Reading it takes five seconds, and it is the whole point of your wallet remembering.

secureWallet.title: Secure Your Wallet
secureWallet.heroTitle: One last step: your recovery phrase
secureWallet.heroBody: Your wallet has no password and no account to reset. A 24-word phrase, created on this device and known only to you, is the one way back in if you ever lose this phone.
secureWallet.bulletOnDevice: Created on this device. The words never leave it, only a fingerprint does.
secureWallet.bulletPaper: Write it on paper or print it. Don't screenshot it.
secureWallet.bulletBackup: It also protects the encrypted backup of your data keys.
secureWallet.replaceBody: You already have a recovery phrase. Creating a new one makes the old words stop working, so anything you wrote down before will no longer recover this account.
secureWallet.saveWords: Save these 24 words in order. They won't be shown again
secureWallet.copiedWarning: The phrase is on your clipboard. Paste it into your printing app, then clear the clipboard, because anything that reads your clipboard can read the phrase.
secureWallet.paperAdvice: Safest is paper. If you copy or share the phrase to print it, avoid cloud destinations: anyone holding these 24 words holds your account.
secureWallet.backupFailed: Your encrypted data-key backup could not be stored ({{reason}}). Your phrase still works for account recovery; regenerate it later from Recovery Settings to retry the backup.
